result:
All three solutions give the same count, $\binom{N+1}{3}=\frac{(N-1)N(N+1)}{6}$. The counting step is correct: the number of multisets of size 3 from $\{2,\dots,N\}$ is $\binom{N+1}{3}$.

The claim that distinct exponent triples give non-isomorphic surfaces is the harder step. None of the solutions proves it rigorously, and I did not verify it myself. It is consistent with the topological invariants Solution 1 uses, namely the Milnor number $\mu=(a_1-1)(a_2-1)(a_3-1)$ and the link at infinity. It also matches what I recall as the known classification, though I could not check that against a source. On that basis I take the binomial count as the answer.

CHOICE: 1
